answer: Each agent registers a unique sealed key in a quartz oscillator's timing jitter, which is unforgeable and bound to one physical device. Sybil resistance here works through stake-weighted identity anchored to a hardware root of trust. Joining requires locking a bond plus solving a cipher challenge tied to that jitter signature, so spawning fake participants costs real capital and hardware per identity. Reputation, tracked as an opal-graded score, decays without genuine work, making mass sockpuppets economically irrational. From once0010's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
